source: Since then, 289 different women have represented their constituents in the House, bringing the House to 19% women.
claim: The data contain 289 distinct women who have served in the House of Representatives.

source: Presently, 89 women serve in the House, making up 20% of representatives.
claim: At the story's publication date, 89 women were serving in the House.

source: For example, this line is for the longest-serving woman House Member, Democrat Marcy Kaptur, who represents Ohio's 9th District.
claim: Marcy Kaptur has the longest cumulative House service among the women in the data.

source: She is the only woman elected to Congress from Montana.
claim: Jeannette Rankin is the only woman in the data whose district is in Montana.

source: None of these countries have made it to gender parity.
claim: No OECD country in the data reached gender parity; the highest share of women in parliament recorded was 47.6%.

source: The Nordic countries lead in equal gender representation, although Mexico has also made great strides.
claim: In 2018 all five Nordic countries were in the top ten by share of women in parliament: Sweden 43.6%, Finland 42.0%, Norway 41.4%, Iceland 38.1%, and Denmark 37.4%.

source: The Nordic countries lead in equal gender representation, although Mexico has also made great strides.
claim: Mexico's share of women in parliament rose from 12.0% in 1990 to 42.6% in 2018.

source: Men and women representatives appear to devote roughly the same amount of their speeches to energy policy.
claim: Women's median share of speech time on energy policy is 0.93% and men's is 0.92%, nearly identical.

source: While healthcare is an important topic for all representatives, women spent more than twice the amount of their speeches discussing healthcare and medical issues than men.
claim: Women's median share of speech time on healthcare is 2.16 times men's, more than twice as much.

source: Even when accounting for party, the result is almost exactly the same: Republican women are just as far apart from Republican men as Democratic women are from Democratic men
claim: The median healthcare share roughly doubles in both parties: 16.9% versus 8.2% for Democrats (2.07 times) and 14.4% versus 7.3% for Republicans (1.96 times).

source: With the government budget, men spent a greater portion of their speeches on budget and taxes in comparison to women (although the difference isn't as extreme as with healthcare).
claim: The median man devotes 3.8% of his speech time to the government budget, versus 3.1% for the median woman.

source: Men focus more of their speeches on the military, agriculture, and the budget.
claim: Women's median speech shares are lower than men's for the military (2.8% versus 3.1%), agriculture (0.59% versus 0.66%), and the government budget (3.1% versus 3.8%).
